correctness.rationale: Each original vertex and its k private leaves forms a disjoint block of weight at least two: empty center forces all k leaves positive, singleton center forces all k leaves positive, double center allows empty leaves. Equality for k>=3 forces double center and empty leaves globally. For k=2 an empty center with two singleton leaves is also possible. Empty centers form an independent set J of G; a nonisolated empty center has four ordered singleton-pair choices (neighbor double centers see both colors), while an isolated empty center has two opposite-color choices. This gives Q_{G,2}(t)=(1+2t)^i I_{G-Z}(4t), and unique Q_{G,k}=1 for k>=3. Exact counting #P-hardness on bipartite 2-leaf coronas uses clone blow-ups G^(r) and I_{G^(r)}(4)=I_G(5^r-1), followed by polynomial interpolation of degree <=n; verifier for oracle witnesses is polynomial. All labels on private leaves are distinguished. Independent check: Independently enumerated all possible local weight-2 block labelings, then tested global OI-rainbow adjacency and independence directly on all base graphs of size <=3 and six representative four-vertex bases for k=2, and small k=3 cases. Observed optimum weight-2n profiles equal the claimed polynomial, including isolated vertices, and k>=3 uniqueness. The logical necessity of the local weight bound proves no lighter function exists for arbitrary G.

originality.rationale: The scalar optimum 2n was known in Samadi–Soltankhah for nonisolated base graphs; it is explicitly not claimed new. Their Theorem 3.4 and Cabrera-Martínez concern minimum weights and corona classes, not the complete optimizer enumerator, the precise isolated-base factor (1+2t)^i, or the specialized #P-hard counting dichotomy. Earlier independent-set counting hardness is credited as an ingredient.
residual_risks: Unindexed specialized corona enumerations could already give the same independent-set polynomial.
The Provan–Ball premise and exact Turing reduction are not claims of parsimonious or bounded-degree hardness.
The k=1 class and full nonminimum enumeration remain outside the theorem.
